rejected_model_findings.title: Passing rent appears to include vacant units, so it is not in-place income

evidence.reason: quote not found on the cited page
quote not found on the cited page

rejected_model_findings.why: The OM labels AED 9,191,500 as 'passing rent' and builds NOI and the 6.91% yield on it. The rent-roll check found that this total equals the potential rent. In-place rent on let units equals the same figure even though 7 units are vacant, 2 have notices served and 2 are in legal cases. So the passing rent seems to count vacant units at asking rent. If so, NOI and the yield are overstated. The OM also gives 117 units, where the rent roll has 116.
rejected_model_findings.analyst_action: Ask for the dated rent roll with a contracted rent for each let unit. Rebuild in-place rent from let units only, with vacant units at zero. Reconcile the 117 units in the OM to the 116 on the roll. Recompute NOI and yield from that figure.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: the deal is blocked on basic facts we do not have (asset type, title, whether it sits in a mandate area, and the minimum and maximum price tests), and nothing else matters until they are resolved.

Legal must confirm freehold single title first. The OM's title statement could not be verified. The price is also unknown, so we cannot test it against the AED 30m [[mandate.min_price_aed.threshold]] floor or the AED 200m [[mandate.max_price_aed.threshold]] ceiling. There is no walk-away price and no buy recommendation. Any later price and returns will rest on the firm's house view, not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Tamarind Residence, completed 2018 [[deal.completion_year]]. The area is not confirmed. The rent roll shows 116 units [[rr.unit_count]]: 64 1BR [[rr.1br.units]], 36 2BR [[rr.2br.units]] and 16 studios [[rr.studio.units]].
- **Price:** not known. The OM's asking price and price per sq ft failed verification and were not used.
- **Income:** in-place contract rent is AED 9.2m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] across 109 let units [[rr.let_units]] and 7 vacant [[rr.vacant_units]]. That is 94% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy by units and 95% [[rr.occupancy_by_area]] by area. Of the let units, 105 are occupied [[rr.status.occupied]], 2 are on notice [[rr.status.notice_served]] and 2 are in a legal case [[rr.status.legal_case]]. The OM's lease structure failed verification, so lease expiries are unknown.

Unit count and building age pass the mandate. Unit count sits within 30 [[mandate.min_units.threshold]] to 250 [[mandate.max_units.threshold]], and completion is after the 2008 [[mandate.min_completion_year.threshold]] cut-off. There is no master lease to a related party.

## Returns
Not underwritten. Asset type, area, title and price are unknown, so there are no returns to show. The yield, IRR, equity multiple and expiry tests against the mandate cannot be run.

## What would make it fail
- Title is not freehold single title, or the buyer is not eligible to own the plot. This ends the deal.
- Asset type, area or price falls outside the mandate once confirmed.
- The OM's headline net yield is overstated, so the real yield on our basis is lower (see Discrepancies).
- Income quality is weaker than 94% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy suggests. Some let units are on notice or in a legal case, and expiry concentration is untested.

## Discrepancies
1. **Title (high).** The mandate requires freehold single title. The OM's title statement could not be verified because the quote was not found on the cited page. The screen relied on nothing here; legal must confirm. Until then nothing else about the deal matters.
2. **OM yield basis (medium).** The OM's headline net yield of 6.91% [[disc.other_om_claim.why]] uses operating costs from a mix of actual, forecast and budget years. The OM says it is before vacancy and collection allowances, and that the figures came from the vendor and were not verified. The yield is likely overstated against a buyer's underwriting. We have no buyer-basis yield to compare it with, because the deal was not underwritten.

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Checks before diligence
- Confirm asset type, area and price, and get legal confirmation of title. These block everything else.
- Title: get the title deeds and DLD ownership records. Legal to confirm freehold status and any nationality restriction.
- Request audited or actual 12-month income and expenditure statements with service charge and chiller reconciliations. Rebuild NOI with vacancy and collection allowances on a like-for-like basis.
- The rent roll is dated 15 September 2026 [[rr.as_of]], 67 days [[notice.stale_rent_roll]] before the screen date. Ask for a current roll before relying on occupancy and expiries.
- Vacant units show no asking rent on the roll. Ask the vendor why.
- Tenant security deposits transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Cheque profile: 18% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is on the most cheques, which means more collection risk. Review it.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including buyer eligibility.
- Building completion certificate from Dubai Municipality.
- Affection plan and permitted use: residential use and floors match the building.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
- Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.

## Assumptions
No house-view assumptions (exit yield, rent path, vacancy, leverage, debt sizing) were applied, because the deal was not underwritten. Any later walk-away price and returns will rest on the firm's house view of rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime. The OM fields that failed verification (asset type, area, title, unit count, price, income, costs, yield and lease structure) were not used. Only the rent roll and the mandate thresholds feed this memo.
